tip: без (bez = without) takes the genitive case, so сахар (sakhar) shifts to сахара (sakhara) here.
For a time of day Russian uses the instrumental with no preposition: вечером (vecherom = in the evening).
до (do = until, up to) takes the genitive, so вечер (vecher) becomes вечера (vechera) here.
For weather, идти (idti) means 'to fall': шёл снег (shyol sneg = snow was falling), literally 'snow went'.
через (cherez = through) plus a time span means 'after, in': через час (cherez chas = in an hour).
из (iz = out of) takes the genitive, so магазин (magazin) becomes магазина (magazina) for 'from where'.
к (k = toward) takes the dative and is the 'to' used for people: к врачу (k vrachu = to the doctor).
несмотря на (nesmotrya na = despite) takes the accusative: несмотря на дождь (... na dozhd = despite the rain).
во время (vo vremya = during) takes the genitive, so урок (urok) becomes урока (uroka) here.
After когда (kogda = when) about the future, Russian uses the future tense: приду (pridu = I will come), not present.
Negated быть (byt) takes the genitive: не будет ответа (ne budet otveta = there will be no answer), ответ (otvet) shifting to ответа.
In a passive, the doer goes in the instrumental: починен моим отцом (pochinen moim ottsom = fixed by my father).
благодаря (blagodarya = thanks to) takes the dative, not the genitive: благодаря тебе (... tebe = thanks to you).
с, со (s, so = off a surface) takes the genitive: стол (stol) becomes со стола (so stola = off the table).
согласно (soglasno = according to) takes the dative: согласно плану (... planu = according to the plan).
в отличие от (v otlichie ot = unlike) takes the genitive: в отличие от брата (... ot brata = unlike the brother).
если (esli = if) marks a real condition; don't confuse it with ли (li = whether) for indirect questions, as in придёт ли он (pridyot li on = whether he'll come).
над (nad = above) takes the instrumental: над диваном (nad divanom = above the couch).
